newsitem.title: USA: Black & Decker stock hit by earnings warning.
newsitem.headline: Black & Decker stock hit by earnings warning.

text.p: The stock of Black & Decker Corp. plummeted Tuesday after the maker of power tools and household appliances warned that its earnings for the fourth quarter and the full year will be disappointing.
Black & Decker tumbled $6.25 to close at $31.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Salomon Brothers, which had previously recommended buying the stock, downgraded it from hold, contributing to the sell-off.
"I'm trying to figure out whether a $6 decline is enough," said Ken Gassmann, an analyst with Davenport & Co. in Richmond, Va. "I love this company, but do I love it at $31?"

The Towson, Md.-based company said its profits will fall short of Wall Street's estimate of $1.00 per share in the fourth quarter. It also said it would not meet expectations of full-year income of $2.40 per share due to lower-than-anticipated sales of power tools and accessories.
Black & Decker also said the earnings growth erosion would continue into the first quarter of 1997, with income down from a year earlier.
The company reported profits of $55.7 million, or 59 cents a primary share, on sales of $1.2 billion in the third quarter.
The company said its Power Tools and Accessories business was hurt by weak economies in Europe.

"Despite substantial cost reductions implemented there during 1996, we were unable to leverage an improved cost base with as much sales growth as we had hoped," it said. "We are beginning, however, to see some improvement in European markets, and our new products are doing well."

The company said it was "optimistic" that the rate of sales growth will increase through 1997. "We also expect to benefit next year from significant incremental cost savings associated with our ongoing European restructuring programme," it added.
